title: introduce-regional-fallback-conductor-and-soft-shed-policy
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: During recent regional congestion incidents we saw oscillating circuit opens and heavy client retries that caused timeout storms and cascading failovers. This PR adds a new runtime component called the 'fallback conductor' that centralizes regional soft-fallback decisions, coordinates ephemeral soft-shedding windows, and introduces a light-weight 'surge-batcher' to reduce per-token overhead during transient bursts. The goals are: 1) stop flip-flopping circuits by tempering reopen attempts, 2) reduce global amplification from retries by applying short, observable soft-sheds per-tenant/route, and 3) batch logically compatible low-latency requests for modest cost savings without impacting SLOs.

What this changes (high level): - runtime/fallback_conductor: new component that tracks regional health signals (latency percentiles, error-rate, queue-depth) and emits timed soft-shed directives with associated grace windows and recovery backoffs. - policy/config: adds config/fallback_policies.yaml with sane defaults for hosted,dedicated,private tiers and per-tenant overrides. - transport/surge_batcher: a lightweight batching path that groups small streaming start events into short-lived micro-batches (<=10ms delay) when soft-shed is active and latency SLOs allow it. - circuit-tempering: improved reopen policy that uses half-life cooling to avoid rapid reopen/reclose cycles and logs audit events for visibility. - telemetry: new metrics and diagnostic traces to measure soft-shed adoption, dropped-by-policy, batch hit-rate, and tempering events. - docs/ops: operational runbook and playbook under docs/operational/fallbacks.md.

Checklist: - [x] Design review (ENG-5892) - [x] Unit + integration tests for conductor and batcher - [x] Load test scenario covering regional spike + reopen noise - [x] SLO evaluation with synthetic production traces - [x] Backwards compatible default config - [x] Release notes entry

Rollout plan: feature is behind a runtime flag (fallback_conductor.enabled). Default off for existing customers; on for internal canary and a small set of customers in us-west-2 for observation. If metrics show unintended impact we will toggle to 'monitor-only' and revert within 2 hours if error-rate rises >0.3% relative to baseline.

review_comments: Arjun Patel (2025-11-08): Can you clarify the soft-shed semantics for streaming requests vs non-streaming? Concern: batching may add latency for the first token. Maya: surge_batcher is gated by a latency budget check; streaming start tokens are only batched when p50 + budget < configured_slo. Added tests and an explicit config flag for aggressive_batching.

Sofia Martinez (2025-11-09): The tempering half-life constant needs reasoned defaults. Suggested making it a percentile-based backoff instead of fixed ms. Maya: switched to exponential half-life tied to incident duration metric; documented in config with examples.

Ben Carlson (2025-11-10): Please add an emergency-off path that can be triggered from Console + API. Maya: added feature_flags.go integration and a Console toggle in the canary deploy config; updated runbook for operator steps.
CI bot (2025-11-11): Integration tests flaked in surge_batcher harness, rerunning. Maya: fixed race in batcher shutdown path and re-ran tests. All green.
Arjun Patel (2025-11-12): LGTM after addressing tests and docs. Approving.
release_notes: Add runtime 'fallback conductor' to coordinate regional soft-fallbacks, a configurable soft-shed policy per deployment tier, a low-latency surge-batcher to group compatible requests, and circuit tempering to reduce reopen oscillations. Feature behind runtime flag for staged rollout.
operational_impact: New metrics and runbook. Default disabled for existing customers; operators should monitor: fallback_conductor.soft_shed_rate, surge_batcher.batch_latency_ms_p95, circuit_temper.events. Canary rollout planned in us-west-2.
post_deploy_actions: Enable feature flag for internal canary, run loadtest scenario, monitor SLOs for 6 hours, then expand to small customer cohort. If errors spike, toggle to monitor-only and notify SRE channel.
notes_for_backport: Backport recommended for release/* if a regional incident indicates reopen oscillation is contributing. Backport will exclude surge_batcher (opt-in) to reduce behavioral risk.
